title: Course Schedule II
hints: Model courses as nodes and each pair [a, b] as a directed edge b -> a. A valid order exists exactly when this graph has no cycle. Which course can always be taken first?

Kahn's algorithm: compute in-degrees, start a queue with every course of in-degree 0, and repeatedly pop one, append it to the order, and decrement its dependants' in-degrees, pushing those that reach 0.
If the order ends up shorter than num_courses, the leftover courses sit on or behind a cycle: return []. A three-colour DFS also works, but on 10^5 nodes it needs an explicit stack in Python.
